title: Vedic Astrology
short_description: A reading of your birth chart in the Jyotish tradition, covering planetary periods and timing questions such as career and marriage.
intro: Vedic astrology, or Jyotish, is one of the oldest systems of astrology still in practice. A consultation uses your date, time and place of birth to prepare a chart, which then becomes the starting point for a structured conversation about the areas of life you want to think through.
what_is: Jyotish maps the positions of the planets and lunar mansions (nakshatras) at the moment of birth. Practitioners read the chart through houses, signs, planetary periods (dashas) and transits. It is a traditional interpretive framework, not an empirical science, and a good consultation is clear about that.
process: Dr. Anameka prepares your chart in advance, studies the questions you have shared, and reads the chart with those questions in mind. The session focuses on your priorities rather than a general recitation of every placement.
who_for: People at a crossroads in career, relationships or family life; those asking timing questions such as career moves or marriage; and anyone who values traditional Indian knowledge systems as part of how they plan.

procedure.title: Share your birth details
procedure.body: Date, exact time and place of birth. If the time is uncertain, mention it so the reading can account for that.

procedure.title: Tell us your questions
procedure.body: Two or three focused questions make for a far more useful session than a general reading.

procedure.title: Consultation
procedure.body: An unhurried session online or in person, with time for your follow-up questions.

procedure.title: Summary and suggestions
procedure.body: Key observations and any optional practices discussed are summarised so you can refer back to them.

benefits: A structured way to reflect on decisions and timing
Time with an experienced practitioner who listens to your situation
Suggestions that are practical and optional, never coercive
limitations: Astrology is a traditional belief system; outcomes are not guaranteed
It does not replace medical, legal, financial or psychological advice
Accuracy depends on the accuracy of the birth time provided

faqs.q: What details do I need for a Vedic astrology consultation?
faqs.a: Your date of birth, the most accurate time of birth you have, and your place of birth. A list of the questions you most want to explore helps the session stay focused.

faqs.q: What if I don't know my exact birth time?
faqs.a: Let us know when you book. Some observations depend heavily on birth time, so the consultation will say which parts of the reading are less certain.

faqs.q: Can astrology predict exactly what will happen?
faqs.a: No responsible practitioner can promise that. Consultations are offered as guidance and reflection, and the decisions remain yours.

faqs.q: Is the consultation available online?
faqs.a: Yes. Consultations can be held online or in person, whichever suits you.

seo_title: Vedic Astrology Consultation | Dr. Anameka S Panda
seo_description: Personalised Vedic astrology (Jyotish) consultations with Dr. Anameka S Panda, online or in person. Thoughtful birth-chart guidance for career, family and life decisions.

title: Vastu Consultation
short_description: Guidance on the layout, orientation and use of homes and workplaces according to the principles of Vastu Shastra.
intro: Vastu Shastra is the traditional Indian discipline of space and architecture. A Vastu consultation looks at how a home, office, shop or factory is oriented and arranged, and offers suggestions for planning new spaces or adjusting existing ones.
what_is: Vastu considers directions, the placement of rooms and entrances, the flow of light and movement, and the use of the five elements. Suggestions can range from planning advice for new construction to simple rearrangements in an existing space.
process: The consultation begins with a floor plan and the orientation of the property. Dr. Anameka reviews the layout, discusses how the space is actually used, and identifies the areas that matter most to you.
who_for: Families planning, buying or renovating a home; business owners setting up offices, shops or factories; and anyone who wants their space to reflect Vastu principles.

procedure.title: Send the floor plan
procedure.body: A floor plan with the north direction marked, plus photographs if available.

procedure.title: Discuss your priorities
procedure.body: Explain how you use the space and what concerns you most.

procedure.title: Site review
procedure.body: An online review of plans and photographs, or a visit where offline consultation is arranged.

procedure.title: Recommendations
procedure.body: Prioritised suggestions, separating simple adjustments from larger changes.

benefits: Clarity on how Vastu principles apply to your specific space
Prioritised suggestions you can act on gradually
Useful input at the planning stage, before construction costs are committed
limitations: Vastu is a traditional discipline; specific outcomes cannot be guaranteed
Structural, electrical or legal matters must always be checked by qualified professionals
Recommendations depend on the accuracy of the plans shared

faqs.q: Do I need to demolish or rebuild to follow Vastu?
faqs.a: Usually not. Many suggestions involve placement, usage and arrangement. Where structural change is discussed, it is presented as an option, and non-invasive alternatives are explained.

faqs.q: Can Vastu consultation be done online?
faqs.a: Yes, using floor plans, the north orientation and photographs. Site visits can be arranged for offline consultations.

faqs.q: Is Vastu only for homes?
faqs.a: No. It is applied to offices, shops, clinics, factories and other commercial spaces as well.

title: Graphology
short_description: Handwriting analysis that looks at how you write as a starting point for self-reflection.
intro: Graphology is the study of handwriting: its size, slant, pressure, spacing, margins and letter forms. A consultation uses these features as prompts for a conversation about personal tendencies and patterns.
what_is: Graphologists observe recurring features of handwriting and interpret them within a structured framework. Its scientific validity as a personality measure is debated, and it should not be used as the sole basis for decisions such as hiring.
process: You provide a sample of natural handwriting on unruled paper. Dr. Anameka studies the sample before the session and then discusses her observations with you, inviting your own reflections.
who_for: Individuals interested in self-reflection; students and parents, as part of Anameka's student programmes; teachers who want another lens for understanding pupils; and anyone interested in handwriting as a personal practice.

procedure.title: Write a sample
procedure.body: Half a page to a page of natural writing on unruled paper, with your usual pen, plus your signature.

procedure.title: Send it
procedure.body: A clear photograph or scan works for online consultations.

procedure.title: Analysis session
procedure.body: Observations are discussed with you, not delivered as a verdict.

procedure.title: Follow-up
procedure.body: Where useful, the session may lead into graphotherapy exercises.

benefits: An engaging, structured prompt for self-reflection
No birth details required
Can be combined with graphotherapy practice
limitations: Graphology is not a validated psychological assessment
It cannot diagnose health or mental health conditions
Should not be used as the sole basis for employment or legal decisions

faqs.q: How should I prepare a handwriting sample?
faqs.a: Write naturally on unruled paper about half a page to a page, using your normal pen and pace, and sign at the end. Avoid copying text or writing unusually neatly.

faqs.q: Can graphology diagnose illness?
faqs.a: No. Graphology is not a medical or diagnostic tool, and any health concern should be taken to a qualified doctor.

title: Graphotherapy
short_description: Guided handwriting exercises practised over several weeks, as a mindful habit-building routine.
intro: Graphotherapy builds on graphology. It involves practising specific changes to handwriting through regular, short exercises, often over a period of several weeks.
what_is: Practitioners of graphotherapy suggest that consciously practising particular strokes and letter forms can support intention-setting and habit change. The approach is traditional and anecdotal; it is best understood as a mindful practice rather than a clinical therapy.
process: After a handwriting analysis, a small number of exercises are chosen. You practise them daily for a set period, with check-ins to review progress and adjust the exercises.
who_for: Students preparing for exams (see the Exam Ready From the Inside programme), people who enjoy structured daily practices, and anyone wanting a calm, focused routine as part of personal growth.

procedure.title: Initial analysis
procedure.body: Graphotherapy starts with a handwriting analysis session.

procedure.title: Exercise plan
procedure.body: A short set of exercises suited to your goals.

procedure.title: Daily practice
procedure.body: Usually a few minutes each day over several weeks.

procedure.title: Review
procedure.body: Check-ins to compare samples and adjust the plan.

benefits: A calm, mindful daily routine
Visible changes in handwriting with regular practice
Accountability through scheduled reviews
limitations: Graphotherapy is not a substitute for medical or psychological treatment
Results depend on consistent practice and vary between individuals
Not a validated clinical therapy

faqs.q: How long does graphotherapy take?
faqs.a: Programmes usually run for several weeks of short daily practice. The exact period is agreed after the initial analysis.

faqs.q: Is graphotherapy suitable for children?
faqs.a: Children can practise handwriting exercises with a parent's involvement. It should complement, not replace, any support recommended by teachers or health professionals.
